title: WebSec Bounty Policy
description: Machine-readable encoding of a bug bounty program's rules: scope, exclusions, known issues, severity floors, PoC requirements. The final gate answers 'is this submission-ready against THIS program', not merely 'is this a real bug'.

asset_weight_usd.description: total assets in scope, for impact calibration

exclusions.description: known issues and excluded behaviors — each is a tripwire for the final gate

pattern.description: substring/keyword matched against finding class, title and description

reference.description: URL or note documenting the exclusion

accepted_risks.description: documented, program-accepted risks (IMPROVEMENTS A1): a matched finding is recorded (finding.bounty.accepted_risk), stays visible and counted, but is not submittable as a vulnerability; a same-pattern exclusion is suppressed (the accepted risk is the narrower, more specific rule). min_severity caps the acceptance: at that severity and above the acceptance does not apply.

pattern.description: substring/keyword matched against finding class, title and description (same semantics as exclusions)

reference.description: URL or note documenting the acceptance

reference_url.description: the program page / scope clause the exclusion cites — G7 hygiene: a policy claim without a reference is still valid but the report stamps it (no reference cited)

min_severity.description: the acceptance stops applying at this severity and above — the gate then demands real handling

submission_budget.description: operator precision budget (IMPROVEMENTS A3): caps the report's top-K acceptance table and lets the ranking key be flipped from acceptance likelihood to severity band. Absent = uncapped, ranked by acceptance.

max_findings.description: 0 (default) = uncapped (top 10 rendered); >0 = cap the top-K table at this many findings, with a note line when the cap is reached

rank_by.description: default acceptance: acceptance score descending (disqualified last); severity: band order (critical > high > medium > low > informational), then validated score descending

acceptance_priors.description: G3 calibrated acceptance prior (wPrior): when true, the acceptance score adds the finding's class base rate over the eval store's adjudicated outcomes (bounded ±0.5, thin classes fall back to silent zero). Absent or false = today's score, byte-for-byte.

auto_tune.description: G17 tactic batting average: when true, the planner auto-deprioritizes a lens whose verdict record is deep enough to trust and bad enough to act on (n_planned>=10 and the Wilson upper of confirmed/planned below 0.10) — its unstarted slots demote to park. Absent or false = today's queue, byte-for-byte.

patch_clause.description: what the program wants for a fix. `verification` (default when absent): a patch that provably blocks the fork PoC and all 3 boundary mutations (check12 as it always was). `prose`: a written recommendation on the finding (verification.recommendation, >= 40 chars) clears the clause and the boundary mutations become an advisory line, not a blocker. `none`: the program does not ask for a fix, so nothing is required of the finding. The boundary-mutation record stays in every mode — only its gate authority changes.
